chunks: As for what ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, that he said:

A man does not perform sajdah upon something that the rest of his body is not upon. So this does not contradict the first two reports, because this report conforms to the generality, and its basis is taqiyyah rather than the state of choice.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity for protection
key_terms.الْخَبَرَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَيْنِ: the first two reports mentioned earlier
key_terms.حَالِ الِاخْتِيَارِ: the state of normal choice or unrestricted circumstance
key_terms.مُوَافِقٌ لِلْعَامَّةِ: in agreement with the common position

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars reconcile a hadith about performing sajdah on something different from what the rest of the body is upon?
ai.summary: This report addresses a fiqh issue related to sajdah and explains how it should be understood alongside other narrations. It states that the report is not taken as contradicting earlier narrations because it is interpreted as having been issued in taqiyyah, not as the ruling in a normal state of choice.
